newsitem.title: UK: Tate says rationalisation to restore growth.
newsitem.headline: Tate says rationalisation to restore growth.

text.p: International sweetener and starch group Tate & Lyle Plc, which reported a big drop in first half profits, said on Wednesday cost cutting and rationalisation would help produce profitable growth in the medium term.
The company saw half-year profits before tax and exceptional costs slump to 113.6 million pounds from 168.2 million a year earlier. Sales fell to 2.3 billion pounds from 2.4 billion.
Tate says rationalisation to restore growth

The group took an 83.2 million pound ($136 million) exceptional charge for reorganising its North American activities, the write-down of some operations in emerging markets and also in the animal feed sector.
The results suffered from a tight squeeze on margins in Tate's Staley sweetener business in North America. The company also suffered from sterling's strength to the tune of 17.3 million pounds.
Chairman Sir Neil Shaw said the group expected improved returns from North American starch and sweetener operations in the second half.
He said Staley would perform well relative to its competitors and sugar operations should continue to make good progress.
"The outturn for the second half of the year will benefit from these improvements but is likely to be affected by the continued strength of sterling," he said in a statement.
Tate said as it made more profits from overseas this year it was declaring a foreign income dividend so as not to disadvantage UK non-tax-paying shareholders.
UK tax-paying shareholders will get 25 percent more than its underlying dividend of 5.3 pence a share, unchanged from last year. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
